title: M. tuberculosis as an organism
dek: A slow, acid-fast, lipid-armored actinobacterium whose cell envelope is the point of most first-line drugs and of the stain that still defines the genus in the clinic.
story: Mycobacterium tuberculosis is a member of the M. tuberculosis complex (MTBC): human-adapted Mtb lineages, M. africanum, and animal-adapted species such as M. bovis. It is an obligate pathogen in practice, with no environmental reservoir that matters for control, and a doubling time of ~18–24 hours in rich medium — slow enough that solid culture takes weeks.

The cell envelope is not a Gram-positive wall with extra grease. From the inside out: plasma membrane, peptidoglycan, arabinogalactan, a mycolic-acid monolayer covalently attached to AG, then a spectrum of extractable outer lipids (PDIM, SL-1, TDM) and mannose-capped lipoarabinomannan. That architecture is why the organism is acid-fast: carbol fuchsin survives acid-alcohol where ordinary bacteria destain.

The reference genome H37Rv (4.4 Mb, ~4,000 genes, GC-rich) is a laboratory strain, not a clinical median. PE/PPE families, the ESX type VII secretion systems, and a lipid-heavy metabolome dominate what makes Mtb genetically and immunologically unlike E. coli.
deepTitle: Envelope chemistry that a genomics lab still has to respect
deep: Mycolic acids in Mtb are C60–C90 α-alkyl, β-hydroxy fatty acids. The FAS-I system makes meromycolate precursors; FAS-II elongates them. InhA (enoyl-ACP reductase of FAS-II) is the INH/ETH target. EmbCAB arabinosyltransferases build AG and are the ethambutol target. The covalent AG–mycolate link is why disrupting either layer is cidal or at least bacteriostatic in replicating cells.

Acid-fastness is a physical chemistry test, not a phylogeny. Nocardia can be partially acid-fast. Dead Mtb can still stain. Smear grade (IUATLD/WHO 0 to 3+) is a density statement, not a viability statement.

MTBC lineages (L1–L9 in current human-adapted schemes, with L2/Beijing and L4 abundant in many genomic datasets) differ in mutation rate, PDIM regulation, and sometimes in the prior on resistance. Lineage is a covariate, not a DST result.
M. bovis BCG is intrinsically pyrazinamide-resistant (pncA polymorphism). That single fact has misled more than one person looking at a “TB” genome from a bladder-cancer BCG patient.

visual.caption: Schematic outer-in section of the Mtb envelope. First-line drugs mostly point at this sandwich: INH at FAS-II mycolates, EMB at arabinogalactan, PZA in a cytoplasm that still cares about envelope stress, RIF at RNAP inside.

example.title: Why BCG is a PZA-resistant “TB” genome
example.setup: A urine isolate from an oncology patient is NAAT-positive for MTBC. The genome is M. bovis BCG. pncA carries the characteristic BCG polymorphism. The lab is asked whether this is pyrazinamide-resistant TB.

steps.title: Species, not just MTBC
steps.body: Xpert and many NAATs answer “MTBC present.” They do not distinguish Mtb from BCG. Phylogenetic SNPs or RD deletion patterns (RD1 absent in BCG) do.

steps.title: PZA is already lost
steps.body: M. bovis (including BCG) is intrinsically PZA-resistant because of pncA. Reporting “pncA mutant, PZA-R” as if it were acquired MDR-TB is a category error.

steps.title: Clinical frame
steps.body: This is likely BCG infection or colonization after instillation, not airborne DS-TB. Relabel the problem before building a four-drug backbone.

example.takeaway: Organism identity is part of DST. MTBC ≠ M. tuberculosis sensu stricto.

check.prompt: What does acid-fast staining physically depend on in Mtb?
choices: A Gram-negative outer membrane with LPS
Mycolic-acid-rich envelope that retains carbol fuchsin after acid-alcohol
check.answer: Mycolic-acid-rich envelope that retains carbol fuchsin after acid-alcohol
check.why: Ziehl–Neelsen and fluorochrome stains exploit the lipid-rich envelope. Mtb is not Gram-negative in the LPS sense and does not spore.

whyWrong.A Gram-negative outer membrane with LPS: Mycobacteria have an outer lipid layer, but it is mycolates, not LPS.

check.prompt: INH, after KatG activation, primarily interrupts which layer’s biosynthesis?
check.why: The INH adduct NAD blocks InhA. EmbB is ethambutol. 23S is linezolid. PBPs are β-lactams.

whyWrong.Peptidoglycan cross-linking (PBP target): That is the β-lactam story, and Mtb has BlaC.

check.prompt: In the envelope plate, which layer is the ethambutol target?
check.figureHint: Read the labels from outer lipids down to cytoplasm.
check.why: EmbCAB arabinosyltransferases build AG. RIF is cytoplasmic RNAP. PDIM is not an EMB target.

whyWrong.Outer lipids (PDIM, TDM): Virulence lipids; not where EMB binds.
whyWrong.Plasma membrane only: Too vague, and EMB is an AG story.
